correctness.rationale: A complete 512-word scan produces 148 self-unbordered vertices and 3080 exact compatibility edges. Every valid code is a clique and every inclusion-maximal code a maximal clique. Pivoted Bron–Kerbosch enumeration has an inductive completeness/uniqueness argument; all 62280 output sets are directly rechecked for compatibility and inability to add another admissible word. A separate C++ string-and-set algorithm reproduces the entire 7,338,080-byte canonical catalogue byte-for-byte, not just the histogram. Orbit closure and orbit sizes are directly verified by bit reversal and complementation. Claim is finite, so exhaustive enumeration suffices; no extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: A full size-by-size count of all inclusion-maximal binary length-nine non-overlap codes is not implied by maximum-size bounds, a particular non-expandable construction, or the previously studied top cardinality. Direct examination of the relevant original articles, later construction-family results, and exact-phrase searches did not reveal the present complete histogram or the free-action result. The largest-size coefficient is included for completeness, not advertised as new. Some unindexed exhaustive computations may still overlap.

value.rationale: The earlier non-expandable-code literature motivates the distinction between greedy termination (inclusion maximality) and globally optimal code size. Binary blocklength nine is a documented exceptional optimum-size case. The complete saturation spectrum quantifies every possible terminal design size and its multiplicity, proves a gap at sizes 2 and 3, and determines all 15570 symmetry classes. It supplies substantially more than a witness, an isolated tiny numerical improvement, or recomputation of the known optimum.
